Week in review: How Trump's policies moved stocks » Catch up on the top… 
Catch up on the top industries and stocks that were impacted, or were predicted to be impacted, by the comments, actions and policies of President Trump and his administration with this weekly recap compiled by The Fly: 1. FACEBOOK: Shares of Facebook (FB) rallied on Tuesday as the company's CEO Mark Zuckerberg testified before the Senate Commerce, Science and Transportation Committee in the wake of the Cambridge Analytica data scandal. The executive reiterated that an ad supported service is still the best business model for the company and said Facebook is cooperating with the office of Robert Muller, but was uncertain if the company had received subpoenas as part of the office's investigation. While acknowledging that Facebook must take a more proactive role, Zuckerberg also said he sees areas of potential legislation that he views as worthwhile to consider. The following day, Zuckerberg returned to Capitol Hill. During his testimony the executive told lawmakers he was among the 87M users whose data was improperly shared with a political consultancy, but denied that users do not have enough control over their data on the social media platform. Amid this, The Wall Street Journal reported, citing Facebook VP of global marketing solutions Carolyn Everson, that the company does not expect to see a significant sales impact from the uproar over its users' digital privacy and also does not expect tougher privacy laws to cut into its ad sales. 2. LOCKHEED MARTIN: The Pentagon has stopped accepting most deliveries of F-35 jets from Lockheed Martin (LMT) due to a fight over who will cover costs for fixing a production error, according to Reuters, citing three people familiar with the matter. A Lockheed spokeswoman told Reuters: "Production on the F-35 program continues and we are confident we will meet our delivery target of 91 aircraft for 2018. While all work in our factories remains active, the F-35 Joint Program Office has temporarily suspended accepting aircraft until we reach an agreement on a contractual issue and we expect this to be resolved soon." 3. CHINA TARIFFS: On Tuesday, China's President Xi vowed to open the country's economy further and lower import duties on goods such as cars. U.S. President Donald Trump responded by tweeting: "Very thankful for President Xi of China's kind words on tariffs and automobile barriers...also, his enlightenment on intellectual property and technology transfers. We will make great progress together!" 4. TRANS-PACIFIC PARTNERSHIP: According to media reports on Thursday, Republican Senator Ben Sasse has said that President Trump has designated economic adviser Larry Kudlow and Trade Representative Robert Lighthizer to review whether to rejoin the Trans-Pacific Partnership trade accord. 5. COHEN RAID: Deputy attorney general Rod Rosenstein personally signed off on Monday's FBI decision to raid the office of President Trump's personal lawyer Michael Cohen, the New York Times (NYT) reported, citing government officials. After that news set off speculation on whether the president would fire Special Counsel Robert Mueller, Trump tweeted Thursday morning: "If I wanted to fire Robert Mueller in December, as reported by the Failing New York Times, I would have fired him. Just more Fake News from a biased newspaper!""Week in Review" is The Fly's weekly recap of its recurring series of "Trump Effect" exclusive stories. FB
